1.
Exemption allowed subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

1. This petition has been filed for quashing of FIR No.100/2019 PS Laxmi Nagar under sections 377/498A/354/406/34 IPC on the ground that the parties have settled their disputes vide compromise deed dated 24th December, 2021, which is on record of this Court.

2. Petitioner nos. 1 and 2 and respondent no.2-complaianat are present in the Court and have been duly identified by the Investigating Officer and the counsel.
3. Petitioner no.1 was married to respondent no.2 on 17th December, 2010 and one child was born out of this wedlock, but due to disputes and differences, the marriage was dissolved by mutual consent vide decree of divorce dated 6th April, 2022.
4.
As per the settlement, a sum of Rs.10 lacs is to be paid to the respondent no.2, which amount respondent no.2 confirms having received towards settlement and now nothing is due any further.
She further submits that she has no objection to quashing of the FIR.

5. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR Prashant Gupta & Anr vs The State Govt. Of Nct Delhi & Anr on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131606599/
1 as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, the FIR No.100/2019 PS Laxmi Nagar under sections 377/498A/354/406/34 IPC and proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
It is however made clear that the said settlement will not affect the rights of the minor child in future.
6. Parties shall abide by the terms of settlement.
7. Accordingly, the petition is disposed of.
Pending applications (if any) are disposed of as infructuous.
8. Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.
